Chapter 9: The Role of Teachers and Mentors – Finding Allies.
Sometimes, the right person at just the right moment can change everything, can’t they? For a child working through the ups and downs of foster care and life in institutions, a caring adult isn’t just helpful—they’re a lifeline.
Imagine meeting teachers or mentors who actually see you—not just your situation. People who notice your strengths, even when you can’t. The boy meets adults like this. They look beyond his circumstances and offer encouragement right when he needs it most.
There’s a teacher who notices when he’s having a tough time. She doesn’t get frustrated or judge him for falling behind, or for being the quiet kid in class. Instead, she’s patient. She takes the time to explain things, gently reminding him that he’s capable of so much more than he realizes.
Can you picture how much that means to a child searching for stability? He starts to look forward to her class. There’s comfort in the routine, and real pride in learning something new.
Then, there’s a mentor at his group home who introduces him to books. Suddenly, whole new worlds open up—places he never imagined. The boy begins to lose himself in stories, finding both escape and inspiration within those pages. Reading becomes his safe space, a way to make sense of his own life.
Most people don’t truly realize how powerful it is to have someone believe in you. Imagine what it’s like to have an adult who sees your potential, not just your struggles.
Of course, these relationships aren’t always smooth. There are misunderstandings. Moments of frustration. Times when the boy pushes people away, just out of fear. But the best mentors? They stick around. They’re patient. They weather the storms and keep offering support, even when it’s not accepted right away.
Little by little, the boy learns to trust these adults. He lets their belief in him become a source of strength. And that’s when something important becomes clear—healing isn’t something you do all alone. It happens through connection, through the people willing to stand by you.
So here’s the key takeaway: the encouragement of a teacher, the guidance of a mentor, even just the kindness of a neighbor—these are the building blocks of resilience. And sometimes, finding the right ally is the very first step toward hope.
